thread:
incident-bot: Pager: p95 inference latency > 2s in az1a for inference-service-prod (route: /v1/generate). Rate of long-tail grpc stalls spiked at 10:43 UTC. Autotriggered alert and grace-mode enabled. <link to alert>
Jane D.: I'm on it. shifting to incident channel. Any customer-visible errors reported? :eyes:
MattG: Logs show `tcp_tx_sched_delay` bumps on several hosts, gRPC retransmits and grpc stream stalls. Nodes not OOM, disk IO normal. Suspect NIC tx-scheduler backlog.
Sara N.: Seeing NIC tx-driver backpressure on az1a hosts, kernel tx-sched latency rising ~200-400ms. Likely single-AZ network egress queuing. Routing upstream looks fine.
Tobi S.: Rolling mitigation: enable cross-az fallback for inference route policy to force 20% traffic to eu1/it for now. I'll flip LB weight override. ETA 2m.
Lee C.: Customer success: we have two customers on paid Dedicated clusters in az1a listing degraded responses, started getting support tickets. Notifying them in 10m unless we have full rollback.
Emma P.: Can we circuit-break long streaming sessions and prefer shorter streams? That should free up sockets/KV pressure.
Priya: Oncall handoff incoming in 15m. @Jane D. will you coordinate with platform to spin up spare instances in az1b/az2 and pre-warm models?
Jane D.: Yes. @MattG can you run `kubectl scale` to add 8 replicas in az1b pool and pre-warm with `--kv-warm=true`? Use the spare ephemeral pool.
MattG: Running now. Pushing 8 pods -> pod creation started, pre-warm script fired. Monitoring model load latencies.
Sara N.: LB weight override applied, cross-az fallback shows 18% traffic shift to eu1a, initial latencies improving for those flows.
Tobi S.: Also enabling circuit-breaker on long-lived streams (threshold 30s) via feature-flag on router. Pushing flag -> should trip within 60s.
incident-bot: Action log: LB override by Tobi S. at 10:48 UTC; circuit-breaker flag set by Tobi S. at 10:49 UTC; scale-up requested by Jane D. at 10:50 UTC.
Lee C.: Drafting customer note: short blurb + ETA 30m, we can update once scale completes. Will include mitigation steps and rollback plan.
Priya: Handoff to next on-call @Tobi S. in 10m. I'm staying for post-handoff sync.
Tobi S.: Confirming I've taken the page. Monitoring p95 across az1a -> p95 baseline dropped from 2.4s to 1.1s after traffic shift and circuit-breaker. Still watching.
MattG: New pods in az1b pre-warmed successfully, model readiness healthy. LB draining old az1a instances gradually.
Sara N.: Net telemetry shows tx-sched latency trending down on az1a hosts after partial traffic drain. Still a few tails at 99th percentile, but the impact area narrowed.
Jane D.: Good. Lee, send the customer note now and include that we're routing, adding capacity, and estimate full resolution in 30-45m.
Lee C.: Sent: "We've detected increased latency affecting inference in one AZ. Traffic rerouted and extra capacity added. Engineers are actively resolving; next update in 30m." :email:
incident-bot: Status page draft suggested: "Partial degraded performance in az1a for inference-service-prod; mitigation in progress."
Priya: Add postmortem owner tag to the incident: `eng-runtime` + `netops`. I'll create the incident doc.
Tobi S.: No additional customer-impacting errors observed. Keeping circuit-breaker enabled until backend tx-sched back to baseline for 2 consecutive p95 windows.
MattG: Running a final health check on gRPC error-rate and token throughput. All green for eu1/az1b targets.
Jane D.: Closing escalation. We'll monitor for 2 hours then start RCA. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
__notes: This thread simulates a short incident coordination exchange: automated alert, triage, cross-AZ traffic shift, scaling, circuit-breaker, customer comms, and on-call handoff. Messages intentionally concise and Slack-like.
